hook.en: If an astrologer told a powerful king that a tiger would one day cause his death, what do you think the king would do?

objectives.en: Introduce Kalki and the satirical style
Narrate the prophecy at the prince's birth

narration.en: If an astrologer told a powerful king that a tiger would one day cause his death, what do you think the king would do?

body.en: "The Tiger King" is by Kalki, the pen name of R. Krishnamoorthy, a Tamil writer and freedom-movement journalist. It is a satire: it uses humour, exaggeration and irony to mock the vanity and cruelty of those in power. The ruler is the Maharaja of Pratibandapuram, whose long, grand-sounding title is itself a joke.

We map the main characters around the Tiger King.

say.en: At the centre is the Maharaja of Pratibandapuram, the Tiger King.
The chief astrologer predicts that a tiger will cause his death.
The Dewan, his minister, is anxious to please him.
A high British officer wants to hunt and pose with a tiger.
He marries a princess from a state with many tigers.
His little son's birthday brings the wooden toy tiger.
The tigers are the victims, and the hundredth has its revenge.

title.en: The prophecy and the prince's childhood

body.en: When the prince is only about ten days old, the astrologers predict that he will one day die, and in the story the infant miraculously speaks to ask how. The chief astrologer names a tiger as the cause. The child is brought up in English style, with an English nanny, English tutor and English milk, and becomes king at about twenty.

problem.en: What makes "The Tiger King" a satire?

steps.en: Target: vanity and cruelty of rulers.
Example: the talking infant and the absurd royal title.

answer.en: The story mocks the vanity, arrogance and cruelty of rulers through humour, exaggeration and irony. A talking ten-day-old prince, a ridiculously long royal title and a king defeated by a toy all expose folly by making us laugh.
